#### List:

- Isoflurane structure
- Volatile structure-activity
- Isoflurane metabolism

#### Isoflurane structure:

![](/content/exams/anzca/2005/B/1/prize-image001.jpg){fig-alt="Isoflurane chemical structure showing its halogenated ether backbone"}

#### Volatile structure-activity:

+-----------------+------------------------------------------------------+
| Physicochemical | - H: ↑flammable                                      |
|                 | - F: ↓flammable                                      |
|                 | - CHF~2~ + dry sodalime → carbon monoxide            |
+-----------------+------------------------------------------------------+
| Pharmacokinetic | - C-F: resistant to oxidative metabolism → ↓toxicity |
+-----------------+------------------------------------------------------+
| Pharmacodynamic | - H: ↑potent                                         |
|                 | - F: ↓potent                                         |
|                 | - Cl: ↓potent                                        |
+-----------------+------------------------------------------------------+

#### Isoflurane metabolism:

+---------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Proportion    | - Only 0.2%                                                         |
|               |   - Low solubility                                                  |
|               |   - Many C-F groups → resistance to metabolism                      |
|               |   - Readily excreted by the lungs → less opportunity for metabolism |
+---------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Location      | - Liver                                                             |
+---------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Mode          | - Phase 1: mostly CYP2E1                                            |
+---------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Metabolites   | - Trifluoroacetic acid                                              |
|               | - Fluoride                                                          |
+---------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Excretion     | - Lungs                                                             |
+---------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Toxicity rare | In theory:                                                          |
|               |                                                                     |
|               | - Hepatotoxicity: antibody binds TFA (hapten) + hepatic proteins    |
|               | - Nephrotoxicity: free fluoride → high output renal failure         |
+---------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
